propositions: Reconciler silently reverts operator's local status changes by one pass because the baseline is advanced from the fetch snapshot rather than the post-push snapshot, making `local == baseline` incorrectly mean 'local unchanged' in the window after an outbound status push.

The guard `_suppressed_by_inbound` fires when local equals the stale baseline, suppressing the outbound emit, which allows inbound to clobber with Jira's pre-push value while other fields from the same pass (like description) survive because they differ from baseline and are pushed.

Soft-failed status transitions (unreachable reverse transition, illegal-transition comment-fallback) must not advance the baseline, as that would record a false sync; baseline advance must gate on per-mutation success, not pass exit code.
The defect affects all five inbound-mirrored fields (summary, description, priority, status, assignee) because they share the `_suppressed_by_inbound` guard, not just status alone.

An accountId-resolved assignee push overlays conservatively to avoid fabricating an identity; if the local assignee is held as email/display name, the baseline will not match and the pass falls back to local-wins (safe direction, pinned by test).
